description: Change a keyword: the platforms it is tracked on (platforms: a list, or null for every platform), mute or unmute it, reclassify it (kind), set its classifier context (null clears), or its matching rules (matching: each field optional, an empty list clears one; requiredTerms with requiredMode any|all, excludedTerms with a `*` wildcard at an end, excludedAuthors, caseSensitive, exactPhrase: true for the exact phrase only, false to also match its words close together, subreddits: { only, excluded } for its Reddit posts alone, each list replaced when sent), or its monthly mention cap (cap: { mentions: N }, null removes it; a cap above this month's count resumes a capped keyword at once), or move it to another group (groupId; a 409 when that group already tracks the term), or replace where it collects reviews, App Store, Google Play, Trustpilot or Google Maps (reviewSources: the whole list, [] disconnects them; a newly added app or country brings its last 30 days free), or replace the RSS or Atom feeds it reads (feeds: the whole list of URLs, [] disconnects them; a newly added feed brings its newest 10 matching items of the last 30 days). It also switches comments on or off (comments: { enabled, maxPerPost }; $0.008 per comment delivered). Rules apply to new mentions only. Returns the updated keyword with its stats. On GitHub a keyword also gets events about repositories naming it; matching.repositories chooses them: events (traction: a repository under 30 days old reached 10 stars; stars: a star milestone from 100 up; growth: fast growth in a week; new: every repository created, even with no stars, off by default), minStars and minWeeklyStars (stars gained in 7 days, 25 or more). An event outside the rule is dropped before it is stored, so it is never billed: "repositories about X with 200+ stars gaining 100 a week" is { events: ["stars","growth"], minStars: 200, minWeeklyStars: 100 }.

anyOf.description: A monthly ceiling on what this keyword may be charged for, mentions and comments together. At the cap it stops matching and receiving comments until the first of the next month (UTC), or until the cap is raised or removed. It stays unmuted: it keeps its place and its daily keyword charge; pause it to stop that too.

mentions.description: Charged items allowed per calendar month (UTC): matched mentions plus the thread comments delivered under them. Every match counts, relevant or not, the look-back a new keyword gets included, because every match bills.

cap.description: Replaces the monthly mention cap; null removes it. A cap above this month's count resumes a capped keyword at once, one at or under it pauses it.

comments.description: Comments under this keyword's mentions; omitted fields are untouched (on create: off, 20 per post).

enabled.description: Read the comments under this keyword's relevant mentions, from 30 minutes after each post, as long as its platform's conversations last (a day to a month). Each comment delivered costs $0.008 (comments of fewer than three words are dropped, never billed) (the comments line of the bill). Off by default.

maxPerPost.description: The newest comments of one thread you receive, 20 by default, 100 at most: the ceiling on what one mention's comments can cost. A comment that names the keyword is a mention too, but only among these newest ones, so it is never billed past the ceiling.

anyOf.description: A sentence the classifier reads for this keyword only, on top of the company profile or the group's own description (at most 300 characters): what the term means here, what to ignore. "Arc is our browser; ignore the geometry word." Null clears it.

context.description: A sentence the classifier reads for this keyword only, on top of the company profile or the group's own description (at most 300 characters): what the term means here, what to ignore. "Arc is our browser; ignore the geometry word." Null clears it.

feeds.description: Replaces the feeds this keyword reads; [] disconnects them all (their mentions stay). A feed added here is checked now and brings its newest 10 matching items of the last 30 days; one already listed keeps its place.

url.description: A feed's address (https://forum.example.com/posts.rss), or a page's (https://forum.example.com): the feed the page advertises is used.

groupId.description: Moves the keyword to this group (grp_...). A 409 when that group already tracks the term.

kind.description: Reclassify it as brand, competitor or topic.

matching.description: Omitted fields are untouched; an empty list clears one.

caseSensitive.description: true: the term must appear in the case it was typed (RAG, never rag). Default false.

exactPhrase.description: true: only the exact phrase matches. false (default): a multi-word keyword also matches a post holding its words close together, in any order, plurals and spellings (non-profit, nonprofit) included; such a match is kept and billed only when the classifier scores it relevant. A term sent in double quotes sets this to true.

excludedAuthors.description: Posts by these authors are dropped: profile or post links, @handles, u/names, Bluesky DIDs or display names, stored in canonical form like an alert's muted list.

excludedTerms.description: A post containing any of these is dropped. A `*` at the start or the end of an entry is a wildcard (beta.* matches beta.0.1; *bot matches nightlybot).

repositories.description: GitHub only: each field is replaced when sent, kept when omitted; null clears a minimum.

events.description: The repository events this keyword takes. traction: a repository created in the last 30 days reached 10 stars. stars: one with 100 stars or more passed a milestone (100, 250, 500, 1,000, 2,000, 5,000 ...). growth: it gained stars fast in a week. new: every repository created, even with no stars (off by default: nearly all of them are noise for a broad keyword). Default: traction, stars, growth. Empty: no repository events.

minStars.description: Only repositories with at least this many stars; null for no minimum.

minWeeklyStars.description: Only repositories that gained at least this many stars in the last 7 days (25 or more). It applies to every event, and one whose last week is not known yet does not pass. null: a growth event needs 100 stars and 20% of the repository's stars in a week, the other events need no growth.

requiredMode.description: any: at least one required term must appear. all: every one must.

requiredTerms.description: The post must ALSO contain these terms, any one of them or all of them per requiredMode. Empty: no requirement.

subreddits.description: Reddit only, for this keyword alone: each list is replaced when sent, kept when omitted.

excluded.description: Replaces the keyword's deny list; [] clears it.

only.description: Replaces the keyword's allowlist; [] clears it.

muted.description: A muted keyword stops polling and matching; its mentions stay.

platforms.description: Replaces the platform list; null means every platform, [] none (reviews only, when the keyword has reviewSources).

reviewSources.description: Replaces the list of apps whose reviews this keyword collects; [] disconnects them all (their reviews stay). An app or country added here gets the free 30-day look-back; one already listed keeps its place.

items.description: A review page whose reviews become this keyword's mentions: its link, or the platform and the id.

countries.description: App Store and Google Play only: storefronts to read, two-letter codes, at most 20. Default: the one in the link, else us. Each is one more poll a day; the same review seen in two storefronts is one mention. Trustpilot and Google Maps have one page for everyone and take none.

id.description: The id on the platform: the digits after "id" on the App Store, the package name on Google Play, the company's domain on Trustpilot (notion.so), a Place ID (ChIJ...) on Google Maps.

language.description: Google Play only: the language of the reviews to read (en, es, de, pt-BR); Google Play answers one language at a time. Default: the link's hl, else en.

platform.description: appstore (Apple App Store), googleplay (Google Play), trustpilot (a company's Trustpilot page) or googlemaps (a place's Google reviews).

url.description: The review page's link: an App Store or Google Play app (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/notion/id1232780281, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=notion.id), a Trustpilot page (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/notion.so) or a Google Maps place (its full link, or a maps.app.goo.gl share link). Or give platform and id.
